quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #9
										  					
  

35 Questions • Passing Score 30

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: The road turns sharply right, then left.
The road turns sharply left, then right.
The road curves to the left.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road turns sharply right, then left.
questions.explanation: This sign tells you the road ahead will turn sharply to the right and then to the left.

questions.question: What does a good defensive driver do?

options.text: Watches what other drivers are doing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watches what other drivers are doing.
questions.explanation: A defensive driver watches other drivers and expects problems. This helps prevent accidents even if other drivers are distracted.

questions.question: Two solid white lines mark a crosswalk. As a driver, what should you know?

options.text: Vehicles have the right-of-way over pedestrians in crosswalks.
Pedestrians in crosswalks must be given the right-of-way.
No one has the right-of-way in a crosswalk.
Pedestrians must stay out of the way of all traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pedestrians in crosswalks must be given the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: Crosswalk lines show pedestrians where it is safe to cross. You must always stop for pedestrians who are in a crosswalk.

questions.question: You are on a one-way street. An emergency vehicle with flashing lights approaches. What must you do?

options.text: Drive to the nearest roadside and stop.
Speed up and take the nearest exit.
Slow down until the vehicle passes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive to the nearest roadside and stop.
questions.explanation: When an emergency vehicle with flashing lights approaches on a one-way street, move to the nearest roadside and stop.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Trucks are allowed on the bridge ahead.
The bridge allows one-way traffic only.
Only one car can cross the bridge at a time.
The bridge may be too narrow to pass a truck.

questions.correctAnswerText: The bridge may be too narrow to pass a truck.
questions.explanation: This yellow warning sign tells drivers that the bridge ahead may be too narrow to safely pass a truck. Drive carefully.

questions.question: What helps drivers save gasoline?

options.text: Leaving the car running in the driveway.

questions.explanation: Quick stops use fuel to accelerate again. If you look ahead and slow down gradually or change lanes to avoid hard braking, you use less gas.

questions.question: Pedestrians in crosswalks and at intersections always have the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: Pedestrians have the right-of-way at any intersection, whether the crosswalk is marked or not.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the overpass ahead has low clearance. Do not go through if your vehicle is taller than the height shown on the sign.

questions.question: Where can you not park?

options.text: Within 15 feet of a fire hydrant.
Within 50 feet of a railroad crossing.

questions.explanation: It is illegal to park within 15 feet of a fire hydrant, within 20 feet of an intersection, or within 50 feet of a railroad crossing.

questions.question: Which light means you should slow down and be careful at an intersection?
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means slow down, look carefully, and be ready to stop.

questions.question: This sign warns drivers about:

options.text: The right lane ends and traffic must merge left.

questions.correctAnswerText: The right lane ends and traffic must merge left.
questions.explanation: This sign tells you the right lane is ending. All traffic in the right lane must move to the left.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: This is a yellow warning sign with black markings. It tells you that traffic may enter from a side road ahead. Stay alert.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Highway changes ahead and to the right.
Hiking trails ahead and to the right.
Hotel ahead and to the right.
Hospital ahead and to the right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hospital ahead and to the right.
questions.explanation: This sign shows that a hospital with emergency services is located to the right.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: This sign means U-turns are not allowed. Do not make a U-turn where you see this sign.

questions.question: To prevent hydroplaning, you should:

options.text: Keep your tires with good tread depth.
Slow down when driving in rain.

questions.explanation: To prevent hydroplaning, keep tire tread deep and tire pressure correct. Also slow down in the rain. Hydroplaning happens most often at high speeds.

questions.question: To avoid hitting vehicles in your blind spots, you should:

options.text: Turn your head to check your blind spot before changing lanes.
Adjust your rearview mirrors every few minutes.
Honk your horn before turning or changing lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head to check your blind spot before changing lanes.
questions.explanation: Before turning or changing lanes, turn your head and look over your shoulder. Never rely only on your mirrors to check blind spots.

questions.question: What happens when alcohol is mixed with another drug?

options.text: Only the alcohol effect may become weaker.

questions.explanation: Mixing alcohol with another drug can make both effects stronger. For example, one drink with a cold medicine may affect you like several drinks.

questions.question: On long trips, you can prevent drowsiness by:

options.text: Moving your eyes side to side while driving.

questions.explanation: Stop regularly on long trips to rest and stretch. Do this even if you do not feel tired yet.

questions.question: When driving on wet pavement, remember:

options.text: Pavement is most slippery right when rain starts.

questions.explanation: Wet roads are very slippery, especially right after rain starts. Your vehicle sits on a layer of oil, dirt, and water. Slow down when rain is heavy or when water pools on the road to keep your tires from slipping.

questions.question: From top to bottom, traffic lights are arranged:
questions.explanation: On a vertical traffic signal, red is at the top and green is at the bottom. On a horizontal signal, red is on the left and green is on the right.

questions.question: You do not need to allow as much distance when following a motorcycle as when following a car.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles can stop faster than cars in dry conditions. Keep 3 to 4 seconds of distance between your car and a motorcycle so the rider has time to react in an emergency.

questions.question: You should drive below the speed limit when:

options.text: Road or weather conditions are not perfect.
You are entering a highway with other cars.
You are on a four-lane road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Road or weather conditions are not perfect.
questions.explanation: Drive below the speed limit when roads are wet or slippery, when you cannot see well, or when any other condition is unsafe. You can be ticketed for driving too fast for conditions even if you are going the posted speed limit.

questions.question: A driver making a left turn at an intersection must yield to a bicyclist coming from the opposite direction.
questions.explanation: When turning left, yield to oncoming bicycles just as you would yield to oncoming cars. Keep your wheels straight while waiting to turn. Proceed only when the intersection is clear of traffic and pedestrians.

questions.question: When you hear a siren or see flashing lights from an emergency vehicle, you must:

options.text: Slow down until it passes you.
Move to the right side of the road and stop.
Wave for the emergency vehicle to pass.
Merge into the right lane and keep driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the right side of the road and stop.
questions.explanation: Yield to any emergency vehicle using flashing lights or a siren. Move to the right side of the road and stop immediately. If you are in an intersection, drive through it first, then stop on the right side.

questions.question: When driving to an unfamiliar area, you should:

options.text: Rely on road signs to find your way.
Plan your trip before you leave.
Only have a general idea of where you are going.
Always take the most direct route.

questions.correctAnswerText: Plan your trip before you leave.
questions.explanation: Plan your route in advance. Do not start with only a vague idea of where you are going. Check the location on a map before you drive.

questions.question: Which drugs can affect your ability to drive?
questions.explanation: Many drugs can affect your ability to drive safely. This includes illegal drugs and legal prescription or over-the-counter medications. Driving while impaired by any drug is illegal.

questions.question: To stay out of a truck or bus driver's blind spot, you should:

options.text: Do not drive next to them and do not follow too closely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not drive next to them and do not follow too closely.
questions.explanation: Large vehicles like trucks and buses have large blind spots on the sides and rear. Do not drive alongside them and do not tailgate them.

questions.question: You can legally pass on the right side of another vehicle when:

options.text: The vehicle is waiting to turn left and there is a passing lane available.
You can drive off the pavement to do it.
You are on a narrow bridge.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle is waiting to turn left and there is a passing lane available.
questions.explanation: If a passing lane is available, you may pass on the right of a vehicle turning left or waiting to turn left. You may also pass on the right on a multilane road with two or more lanes going the same direction. Never drive off the pavement to pass another vehicle.

questions.question: When it starts to sleet or snow, you should:

options.text: Keep your windshield and mirrors clear.
Stay farther back from the vehicles ahead of you.
Drive carefully around all other vehicles.

questions.explanation: In snow, keep your windshield and mirrors clear. Increase your distance from other vehicles because slippery roads require more distance to stop.

questions.question: You may drive around the gates at a railroad crossing:
questions.explanation: Stop at all railroad crossings when warning signals are active. These signals include flashing red lights, lowered gates, a flagger, or train noise. Never try to go around a lowered gate.

questions.question: What happens when a bicyclist breaks traffic laws?

options.text: It is allowed because bicyclists do not have to follow traffic laws.
Law enforcement will always give them a warning.
Their bicycle will be taken away.

questions.explanation: Bicyclists have the same rights and responsibilities as drivers. Both drivers and bicyclists who break traffic laws can be ticketed.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns that two-way traffic is ahead.

questions.question: When a driver behind you wants to pass, what should you do?

options.text: Slow down to give the other driver room to pass safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down to give the other driver room to pass safely.
questions.explanation: Slow down when someone wants to pass you. This creates space in front of your vehicle so they can pass easily and quickly.

questions.question: Which statement is true?

options.text: Signal at least 100 feet before changing lanes to pass. Make sure no cars are coming.
Use your mirrors and check over your left shoulder for your blind spot when passing left.
Wait until you see both headlights of the other car in your rearview mirror before returning to your lane.

questions.explanation: When passing, signal at least 100 feet before changing lanes. Check your mirrors and look over your shoulder to see your blind spot. Wait until both headlights of the passed car appear in your rearview mirror before moving back to your lane.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Stop only if other cars are coming.

questions.explanation: This sign shows where bicycles cross or ride next to traffic. Drive carefully in this area because bicycles are likely to cross or ride nearby.
